title: Microsoft Purview: auto-expanding archive limit rises to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes in GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: The briefing passes: the government-cloud rollout, eligible licences, archive limits and PowerShell controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes the automatic capacity increase from enabling auto-expanding archiving and reports the differing rollout dates and limits in Microsoft's sources.

claims.claim: The notice schedules General Availability rollout in GCC, GCC High and DoD to begin in mid-November 2026.

claims.claim: The notice expects the government-cloud rollout to complete by early December 2026.

claims.claim: The supplied notice sets no act-by date.

claims.where: What's changing, third paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: Both cited Learn pages give a rollout beginning in mid-October 2026 and expected to complete by late October.
claims.quote: Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October.

claims.where: What's changing, third paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The rollout banner on Learn does not name a cloud.
claims.quote: Microsoft is increasing the maximum auto-expanding archive capacity for eligible Exchange Online mailboxes from 1.5 TB to 3 TB. Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October.

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages still give a 1.5 TB limit in their body text.
claims.quote: This archiving feature in Microsoft Purview (called auto-expanding archiving) provides up to 1.5 TB of additional storage in archive mailboxes.

claims.claim: The additional headroom does not require a support request.
claims.quote: This enhancement helps organizations retain and manage larger volumes of archived email content without requiring manual archive expansion processes or support requests.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says no more data is stored in the auto-expanding archive when it reaches 1.5 TB, the continuing limit for non-eligible licences.
claims.quote: If a mailbox with an auto-expanding archive reaches a total of 1.5 TB of data stored in the auto-expanding archive, no more data will be stored in the auto-expanding archive or moved from the main archive to the auto-expanding archive.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licence assignments for users with large archives.
claims.quote: Review license assignments for users with large archive mailboxes to confirm eligibility.

claims.where: Why it matters, second paragraph; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating documentation, retention guidance and help desk materials.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation, retention guidance, and help desk materials to reflect the new 3 TB limit.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licensing and retention strategies for non-eligible archives.
claims.quote: Review licensing and retention strategies for users whose archive mailboxes are not eligible for the expanded capacity.

claims.where: Why it matters, second paragraph; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The increase does not itself enable auto-expanding archiving; an administrator enables the underlying feature.
claims.quote: An administrator enables auto-expanding archiving for the mailbox.

claims.claim: The documentation describes no new permission or identity for the capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" "3 TB" "permissions". Read MC1521615 and learn.microsoft.com/purview/autoexpanding-archiving and /purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving; existing enablement roles are given, with no new permission or identity for this increase.

claims.claim: eDiscovery tools such as Content Search search the additional storage areas of auto-expanded archives.
claims.quote: When you use an eDiscovery tool, such as Content Search, the additional storage areas in an auto-expanded archive are also searched.

claims.claim: A hold on a mailbox also covers content in its auto-expanded archive.
claims.quote: When you put a mailbox on hold by using methods such as Microsoft 365 retention, eDiscovery case holds, and Litigation Hold in Exchange Online, content located in an auto-expanded archive is also placed on hold.

claims.claim: After auto-expanding archiving is enabled, additional storage is added automatically as needed.
claims.quote: When the archive mailbox gets close to its storage limit, additional storage space is automatically created

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators cannot adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Administrators can't adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement cannot be turned off.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Per-user enablement cannot be turned off.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.claim: For E5 licences, Learn says to verify that Records Management is selected and remains enabled.
claims.quote: For E5 licenses, verify that Records Management is selected and remains enabled in the user's license settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Once an auto-expanded storage area exists, users cannot delete folders from the archive.
claims.quote: If an archive mailbox has at least one auto-expanded storage area, users can't delete a folder from the archive mailbox or from the auxiliary archive.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving prevents recovery or restoration of an inactive mailbox.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving prevents you from recovering or restoring an inactive mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The increased capacity is included for mailboxes assigned a named eligible licence, without a separate per-GB charge.
claims.quote: The increase applies to mailboxes assigned the following eligible licenses: ... If auto-expanding archiving is already enabled, no additional configuration or per-GB charge applies.

claims.quote: The combination of the eDiscovery & Audit, Insider Risk Management, and Information Protection & Governance mini suites

claims.quote: Qualifying offerings that include Microsoft Purview E5 capabilities, such as E7, also support the increase.

claims.claim: The cited Learn archive pages state no price for moving a user to an eligible licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" "3 TB" "price". Read learn.microsoft.com/purview/autoexpanding-archiving and /purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving in full; both name eligible licences and no per-GB charge, but neither quotes a licence-upgrade price.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: The user's archive mailbox must already be enabled before enabling auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: A user's mailbox must already be enabled for archive before you can enable auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports cloud-based archive mailboxes in Exchange hybrid deployments.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment for users who have an on-premises primary mailbox.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving is not supported for on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving isn't supported for on-premises mailboxes in any version of Exchange Server.

claims.claim: There is no documented admin-centre path to enable organisation-wide auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" enable "admin center" "portal". Read learn.microsoft.com/purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving: "You can't use the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auto-expanding archiving. You must use Exchange Online PowerShell."

claims.claim: There is no documented admin-centre path to enable per-user auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" enable "admin center" "portal". Read learn.microsoft.com/purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving: "You can't use the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auto-expanding archiving. You must use Exchange Online PowerShell."

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement requires a global administrator or an Organization Management role-group member.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving, you must be a global administrator in your organization or a member of the Organization Management role group in your Exchange Online organization.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls table
claims.claim: For specific users, membership of a role group including Mail Recipients suffices.
claims.quote: Alternately, to enable auto-expanding archiving for specific users, you must be a member of a role group that includes the Mail Recipients role.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell enables auto-expanding archiving organisation-wide.
claims.quote:
To enable auto-expanding archiving for your entire organization, run the following command:
Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell enables auto-expanding archiving for a specific user.
claims.quote:
To enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user, run the following command.
Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The per-user command requires both primary and archive mailboxes to be cloud-based.
claims.quote: If a user's primary and archive mailboxes are both cloud-based, then you can use the Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive command to enable auto-expanding archiving for that specific user.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: For an on-premises primary mailbox with a cloud archive, enable auto-expanding archiving using the organisation-wide command.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment, you have to run the Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive command in Exchange Online PowerShell to enable auto-expanding archiving for the entire organization.

claims.claim: Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks organisation-level enablement.
claims.quote:
To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks per-user enablement.
claims.quote:
To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for a specific user, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement does not change AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled on individual user mailboxes to True.
claims.quote: Running the Set-OrganizationConfig cmdlet to enable auto-expanding archiving for your organization doesn't change the AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property on user mailboxes to True.

claims.claim: Neither enablement control selects the archive ceiling; the eligible licence determines the increased capacity.
claims.quote: The increase applies to mailboxes assigned the following eligible licenses: ... For all other licenses, the existing 1.5 TB limit remains unchanged. ... Administrators can't adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Per-user enablement for a mailbox on hold or assigned a retention policy adds 10 GB to the archive quota.
claims.quote: When you enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user and the user's mailbox in on hold or assigned to a retention policy ... The storage quota for the user's primary archive mailbox is increased by 10 GB (from 100 GB to 110 GB).

claims.claim: The cited archive pages do not explain what happens to an archive already over 1.5 TB when its eligible licence is removed.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" "3 TB" "license" "removed". Read learn.microsoft.com/purview/autoexpanding-archiving and /purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving in full; they give eligibility and limits but no treatment of an already oversized archive after licence removal.

claims.claim: The capacity increase is on automatically for the eligible, already-enabled mailboxes it targets.
claims.quote: Eligible mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled will continue to grow automatically as needed. ... No action is required if eligible mailboxes already have auto-expanding archiving enabled.

controlChecks.governs: Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation
